title: 30,000 expected to attend rally vs corruption
summary: Around 30,000 people are expected to gather at the People Power Monument on Dec. 9 for an anti-corruption rally organized by the Inter-Religious Leaders Council for National Transformation-White…

blocks.text: Fr. Tony Labiao, WRM executive director, yesterday told The STAR the anti-corruption indignation rally would be a continuation of a similar mass action last year.

MANILA, Philippines — Around 30,000 people are expected to gather at the People Power Monument on Dec. 9 for an anti-corruption rally organized by the Inter-Religious Leaders Council for National Transformation-White Ribbon Movement (ILCNT-WRM).

Labiao said the date of the rally coincides with the International Anti-Corruption Day, adding that their group decided to organize the December rally in response to the prevalence of massive corruption despite the large crowds that turned up during last year’s protest action.

He said the latest push for another protest action was “also triggered by the budget” as reports emerged that some lawmakers attempted new insertions in the 2027 budget program. There have also been reports of new “presidential pork” in the form of Financial Assistance to Local Government Units (FALGU).

“We demand that the investigation on the flood control corruption continue and be fast-tracked, and for those involved in the corruption to return the money that they have stolen from the people. We also appeal that everyone should be made accountable. It should not just be selective accountability,” Labiao said.
The group is also calling for transparency in budget allocations, adding it has tied up with the People’s Budget Coalition.
“We called it a White Ribbon Movement because there is no political color. For as long as you are anti-corruption, you are welcome to attend,” he said.
The inter-religious event will gather followers of the Roman Catholic Church, Philippine Council of Evangelical Churches (PCEC), National Council of Churches in the Philippines (NCCP) and Muslims.
